summary: Build, provision and verify the native development API without replacing stable Shin or touching consumer repositories.
scope: Isolated development commands; current capabilities and remaining holds follow shin-server-development-v1 and shin-stable-carry-forward-v1. Consult executed slice evidence; no global service, skill, remote deployment, Desktop/dashboard or MCP adapter is installed.

verification.profileChecks: Strict, read-only route and evidence checks.
verification.packageChecks: Portable install and relocation are separate from a source build.

journalLifecycle.migration: Journal epochs introduced schema016; P3E20 itself added no database migration. These are historical slice facts, not the current database schema. Resolve the required databaseSchema and configuration template from docs/machine/shin-companion-protocols-v1.json; private checkpoints subsequently require migration017. Use the explicit native migrate command with an absolute private migrator config accepted by check-config. Configuration review is separate and preserves credentials and identity. Do not run this against consumer databases.
journalLifecycle.maintenance: Inspect producer inventory and explicitly retire all observed sequences before requesting GET /api/v1/telemetry/retrieval/journal/epochs/reclamation?through=N. Review every producer identity in the bounded plan. POST the exact plan with discard_future_confirmed=true only to deliberately fence those process lifetimes, including still-running ones. No automatic cleanup is implied.
journalLifecycle.capture: A reclaimed current process reports journal-producer-reclaimed and does not reenroll. Normal retrieval remains available. An explicit process restart creates a fresh lifetime; no request invokes it automatically.
journalLifecycle.verification: Publication integration includes journal_epoch_migration_checks and retrieval_journal_epoch_checks; the native Store probe checks active128 capacity, recovery beyond128 admissions and capture/reclamation interleaving. All run only under the dedicated stand guard.

localObserver.version: See shin-companion-protocols-v1 for the shared Observer protocol identity.

title: Isolated Server Development Commands

journalWriter.configuration: The journal_writer object in the current configuration schema defaults to disabled; currentProtocols owns the schema identity. Explicitly choose a configured administrator, interval_ms, max_retry_ms and flush_on_shutdown before enabling; observability retention must be nonzero. Query payload capture still requires its separate project allowlist.
journalWriter.status: GET /api/v1/telemetry/retrieval/journal/writer is admin-only and read-only. Inspect pending batch, last-polled sequence progress, acknowledged_producer_epoch, retry delay and failure stage/code. Null acknowledged epoch does not prove missing database admission.
journalWriter.shutdown: After HTTP drain the writer joins and logs journal-writer-stopped with bounded status. Optional final flush attempts at most two exports; shutdown_prefix_acknowledged includes known missing sequences and is not all-traffic completeness. Synchronous DB operations retain existing per-operation timeouts, not a hard total shutdown deadline.
journalWriter.verification: Native journal_writer_test and journal_suffix_snapshot; journal_writer_checks in the publication suite; scoped ThreadSanitizer, full Release/instrumented companion gates and a bounded enabled/disabled HTTP sample. No automatic retention or identity rotation.

storeCost.rule: Run only with the existing stand already migrated/current, no Server listener and no concurrent DB harness. This command never provisions/migrates/starts/stops PostgreSQL or Server. It compares full public Store readiness to a raw SELECT 1 transaction lower bound, not isolated schema CPU or product throughput. Reports stay private under the explicit build state.

coreMacStaticAnalysis.rule: Configure this separate directory before passing it to release-check. The compile database and clang-tidy must agree on the compiler/toolchain. The initial P3E17 default Apple compile database/Homebrew tidy pairing could not find standard headers and emitted invalid-AST diagnostic cascades. The consistent LLVM run passed unchanged code and policy; no suppression or destructor rewrite was appropriate. Other platforms use their configured compiler paths, not these Mac bindings.

contextRoute.rule: Use build/cf-perf-core/shin-context with this development worktree as explicit root, after verifying --version and source binding as required by AGENTS.md. The older core-p2, cf2-core and cf34-core artifacts are historical controls, not the current candidate route. Build explicitly, then require check/doctor/eval and current Brief. The focused profile excludes its own golden query definitions from retrieved documents; it does not suppress failures of the broader shin self-profile.
contextRoute.pythonBoundary: The selected Core does not extract Python declarations. Python inputs are freshness-tracked; use the test/tool paths in this workflow to verify their code directly, not an invented member-level fact.

prerequisites: Docker Compose for the isolated PostgreSQL stand
configurePolicy: CMake downloads checksum-pinned cpp-httplib and libpqxx. On other platforms provide normal CMake dependency discovery paths; the native Linux build has not yet been certified for this server slice.

database.retention: down retains the named volume. Deleting the volume or resetting the schema is an explicit destructive development action, not normal server startup.
database.secrets: init generates private random tokens/passwords below build/server-dev, validates existing files and never replaces existing credentials. Do not print or commit the state directory.
database.authentication: The dedicated loopback PostgreSQL uses SCRAM. Generated conninfo explicitly sets gssencmode=disable because this stand has no Kerberos realm; this does not change Core or force off GSS for other configurations. Remote database TLS and enterprise authentication remain separate unvalidated deployment work.
